body: Colony Wars: Red Sun is Psygnosis' PlayStation space-combat game, first released in Europe on 24 March 2000. The third Colony Wars follows a miner who becomes a mercenary, moving away from the military allegiance that defined the earlier campaigns. Available contracts let the player choose which work to undertake before returning to the main story. Battles take place in space and within planetary atmospheres. The change in role gives each mission an additional practical purpose: successful work supplies the money needed to improve the ship that will carry out the next contract.

Nine spacecraft offer different combinations of weapons and capabilities. Money earned by completing missions and destroying targets can purchase new craft or equipment, while predetermined slots limit how the chosen vessel can be configured. Interception and escort assignments ask for different priorities during combat. Large enemy ships also have individual components that can be targeted, making a turret a useful objective within a larger encounter. The player prepares for the job, then reads the battle for opportunities that suit the equipment brought into it rather than firing at every visible target indiscriminately.

Only designated plot missions are required to advance the main story, leaving other contracts available as a way to earn resources and develop the ship. This structure gives Red Sun a more open rhythm than its predecessors without abandoning their cockpit combat. Gary McKill composed the score for the concluding PlayStation entry. Midway handled the delayed North American release later in 2000. Red Sun's distinctive contribution is the connection between choosing work and shaping a vessel: progress depends partly on deciding which available risk is worth taking before the next major story assignment.
